title: Weakly negatively regressive sampling of matroid bases
formal:
Does there exist a uniform randomized algorithm which, for every finite matroid \(M\) on \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) given by an independence oracle and every rational point \(p\) of its base polytope, samples a basis \(B\) with exact marginals
\[\Pr[i\in B]=p_i\quad(i\in[n])\]
and a weakly negatively regressive output distribution, in expected time polynomial in \(n\) and the binary encoding length of \(p\)?

Here weak negative regression (WNR) requires, simultaneously for every \(i\in[n]\) and every increasing function \(f:2^{[n]\setminus\{i\}}\to\mathbb R\),
\[\mathbb E[\mathbf 1_{\{i\in B\}} f(B\setminus\{i\})]\le p_i\,\mathbb E[f(B\setminus\{i\})].\]
The algorithm receives no objective function \(f\). One output law must satisfy all these inequalities.

This card selects WNR, the weakest of the three alternative dependence requirements in the source question. Negative association or negative regression would also suffice by implying WNR. The independence-oracle, rational-input and exact expected-time sampling conventions below make the source's efficiency question precise; they are explicit editorial conventions.
why: Randomized rounding must reconcile combinatorial feasibility with the dependence created by exact marginal requirements. This question asks whether every matroid base point has an efficiently accessible law controlling all monotone effects of conditioning on one coordinate. Such a general sampling theorem would support objective-independent rounding and strong guarantees for nonlinear submodular objectives, beyond the linear expectations fixed by marginals alone.

sentences: The problem asks for efficient sampling of a matroid basis with any prescribed rational point of the base polytope as its exact marginal vector.
The output law must satisfy weak negative regression for every increasing function of all coordinates except one.
The chosen model uses an independence oracle and a uniform exact sampler with expected polynomial bit complexity.
This dependence property implies favorable submodular expectations and supports known concentration guarantees.
A reported gap in an older general-matroid claim remains acknowledged in the 2026 literature, while newer special-case rounding results do not settle this target.

definitions:
A matroid \(M=([n],\mathcal I)\), with \(n\ge1\), consists of a nonempty family \(\mathcal I\subseteq2^{[n]}\) of independent sets. If \(A\in\mathcal I\) and \(A'\subseteq A\), then \(A'\in\mathcal I\). If \(A,D\in\mathcal I\) and \(|A|<|D|\), some \(e\in D\setminus A\) has \(A\cup\{e\}\in\mathcal I\). A basis is an inclusion-maximal member of \(\mathcal I\); all bases have the same cardinality. Let \(\mathcal B(M)\) be their family, including the singleton family containing the empty set for a rank-zero matroid.

The base polytope is
\[P_B(M)=\left\{\sum_{B\in\mathcal B(M)}\lambda_B\mathbf 1_B:\lambda_B\ge0,\ \sum_B\lambda_B=1\right\},\]
where \(\mathbf 1_B\in\{0,1\}^n\) is the incidence vector. This is the convex hull of bases, as specified by the source's maximal-independent-set convention. It is distinct from the convex hull of all independent sets.

An oracle query supplies an \(n\)-bit incidence vector for a set \(A\) and receives the exact bit indicating whether \(A\in\mathcal I\). The oracle is fixed throughout a run and is promised to describe a matroid. The input gives \(n\) in binary and \(p_i=a_i/b_i\), with binary integers \(0\le a_i\le b_i\) and \(b_i\ge1\). Let \(L\) be their total encoding length. The promise is \(p\in P_B(M)\); membership testing is not an additional required output. A convex decomposition of \(p\), an explicit list of bases and a sampling oracle are not supplied.

Use a probabilistic multitape Turing machine with this independence oracle and independent fair random bits. All ordinary bit operations, random-bit generation, oracle-query preparation and output writing count toward time; obtaining the answer to a completed oracle query costs one additional step. There must be fixed constants \(C,d\) such that expected total work is at most \(C(n+L+1)^d\) on every promised input and every matroid oracle. These constants and the machine are independent of the instance. No arbitrary real-arithmetic operations or nonuniform advice are available.

The machine must halt with probability one, and every terminating run must output the incidence vector of a basis. Its probability law over outputs must have the exact stated marginals and satisfy WNR without an additive tolerance. There is no failure output or exceptional probability on which feasibility or the distributional guarantees may fail. Expected time permits exact sampling with rational probabilities whose denominators are not powers of two. Independent invocations use fresh random bits; a joint coupling across different inputs is not required.

Increasing means \(f(A)\le f(D)\) whenever \(A\subseteq D\). The domain is finite, so each real-valued \(f\) has finite expectation. For \(0<p_i<1\), the displayed WNR inequality is equivalent to
\[\mathbb E[f(B\setminus\{i\})\mid i\in B]\le\mathbb E[f(B\setminus\{i\})\mid i\notin B].\]
For \(p_i=0\) or \(p_i=1\), the unconditional inequality is automatically an equality and does not invoke undefined conditional probabilities. WNR concerns all increasing functions of the remaining coordinates, not just pairwise covariances or linear functions.

For context, a set function \(F:2^{[n]}\to\mathbb R\) is submodular when \(F(A)+F(D)\ge F(A\cup D)+F(A\cap D)\) for all sets \(A,D\). Submodular dominance at marginals \(p\) means \(\mathbb E[F(B)]\ge\mathbb E[F(R_p)]\) for every such \(F\), where \(R_p\) includes each element independently with probability \(p_i\). This consequence of WNR is not a substitute for the stronger specified distributional target.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof or refutation of the existence statement in the declared oracle and bit-computation model. A positive answer must establish one uniform sampler, exact feasibility and marginals, all WNR inequalities, almost-sure termination and the expected polynomial resource bound for every promised input. A negative answer must prove that no such sampler exists; it need not show that a WNR law is nonexistent for any individual input. A theorem that only supplies a distribution nonconstructively, approximate marginals, pairwise negative correlation, submodular dominance, or a sampler for a restricted class of matroids does not by itself meet the full criterion.

context_blocks.text: The 2022 question asks about sampling for arbitrary matroid marginals with WNR, negative association or negative regression. The latter two properties each imply WNR. This card adopts the first listed branch and retains arbitrary matroids; it does not impose one particular rounding procedure.

WNR implies submodular dominance: every submodular objective has expectation at least that under independent inclusion with the same marginals. Matching marginals alone fixes linear objectives, but does not establish this nonlinear guarantee.

The source reports a gap in an earlier claimed negative-association sampler for general matroids. It also observes that maximum-entropy matroid distributions need not have the required negative dependence, because even uniform distributions can have positively correlated coordinates.

The 2026 journal paper proves dimension-free submodular lower-tail bounds under one-negative association, equivalent to WNR for binary variables. Its introduction continues to flag the gap in the earlier general-matroid sampling claim and leaves the dependence properties of standard matroid rounding procedures open. These are conditional consequences of the dependence property, not a construction for every matroid.

The 2026 correlated-sampling paper gives cardinality-constrained rounding with preserved marginals and submodular dominance. Its discussion of negative association includes a known hypersimplex sampling law, and the introduction mentions a partition-matroid extension. Cardinality and partition constraints are special cases of matroids; the paper does not establish the arbitrary-matroid target here.
